clue.text: Takes a brighter outlook when fringe benefits increased

parts.note: perks are extras given on top of a salary
up, as in prices being up

explanation.surface: Someone cheers up on hearing their job's perks have been improved.
explanation.definitionFit: To perk up is to become more cheerful and lively.

clue.text: Look closely at sort of shirt taken in with synthetic material

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so the letter for the shirt goes inside

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
a T-shirt is a sort of shirt
a sham is something fake or synthetic

explanation.surface: Examining a shirt that has been altered, made of man-made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' (as a tailor takes in a garment) puts T inside PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded ribbon or heavy woollen cloth.

clue.text: Soldiers detailed for course of exercise

indicators.note: with its tail removed, so the last letter of the word for soldiers goes

parts.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are assigned to a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means given duties, but here is de-tailed: REGIMENT loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed programme, for instance of diet or exercise.

clue.text: Failing to collect the rents initially, fellow gets tough

indicators.note: collecting means gathering inside, so the initials go within the word for failing

parts.note: a failing or moral fault is a sin

indicators.note: taking the first letter of each of the words the and rents

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A landlord who fails to collect rents decides to get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T and R from 'the rents'; 'to collect' puts them in SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and severe.

clue.text: Opening a mineral after parking

indicators.note: the mineral word comes after the parking letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A mine is opened after a car park is built.
explanation.definitionFit: A pore is a tiny opening, as in the skin.

clue.text: Fast food outlet requiring injection of hard cash

definitions.text: Fast food outlet requiring injection of hard cash

parts.words: Fast food outlet requiring injection of hard cash
parts.note: sounds like a struggling restaurant needing investment, but describes an eatery where food is bought by putting coins into a slot

explanation.surface: A burger chain needs a cash injection to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injection of hard cash' reads as business investment; literally it is coins pushed into a machine. An automat was a coin-operated self-service restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: An automat dispenses meals from coin-operated compartments, a vending-machine restaurant.

clue.text: One on the staff, perhaps, but not by choice

definitions.meaning: in music, a sharp, flat or natural sign written on the stave
happening by chance rather than intention

explanation.surface: An employee who ended up in the job by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but it is the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical accidental is a sign altering a note's pitch; the adjective means unintended.

clue.text: A casual individual from The Times

parts.note: a temp is a casual or temporary worker
I is one, an individual

explanation.surface: A freelance contributor from The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper; the answer is the plural of tempo, musical times.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed or time at which music is played.

clue.text: Nautical platform isn't commonly clean outside

indicators.note: the cleaning word stands outside, around the other piece

parts.note: to mop is to clean
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A ship's deck that isn't usually cleaned on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't commonly' points to a non-standard spoken form; 'outside' wraps the cleaning word around it. A maintop is the top of a ship's main mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is the platform at the head of a ship's lower mainmast.

clue.text: Border flower leaving unwanted growth when headed

definitions.text: Border flower leaving unwanted growth when headed

parts.words: Border flower leaving unwanted growth when headed
parts.note: a flower in a garden border suggests a plant, but a flower here is a river on the Scottish Border, and cutting off its head leaves a weed

explanation.surface: A garden plant that turns into a weed once deadheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river; the Tweed runs along the Scotland–England border. Remove its first letter and WEED remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is the river forming part of the boundary between Scotland and England.

clue.text: Dynamic sort in Vortigern's band

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the name Vortigern, running across its middle

explanation.surface: An energetic member of the band led by the ancient British king Vortigern.
explanation.walkthrough: Vortigern was a fifth-century British warlord; the name conceals the answer between VOR and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a fierce, energetic person, as in a tiger in business.

clue.text: On crime, be original to achieve reformation

indicators.note: being original means making something new, so these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reforming criminals requires them to come up with new ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator 'be original' shares the word 'be' with the fodder only in appearance: the fodder is ON CRIME plus the first BE, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To recombine is to join together again in a new way, a kind of re-forming.

clue.text: A traveller taking in two cities

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A wanderer passes through two cities on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romany is a Gypsy, one of a traditionally travelling people.

clue.text: Very fond of supplement to reconstituted diet with cold ingredient

parts.note: to supplement is to add

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a mixture, so the letter for cold goes inside
reconstituted food is made up again, so the letters of diet are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on adding supplements to a reconstituted diet with a chilled ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstituted' rearranges diet to ITED, and 'ingredient' places the cold letter inside, giving ICTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being addicted to something means being hooked on it, extremely keen.

clue.text: Ignores girl's looks

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, plus the possessive s
regards are looks or glances

explanation.surface: Someone takes no notice of a girl's glances.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard is to pay no attention to something.

clue.text: Turn on fellow grabbing gin cocktail

indicators.note: one word grabbing another holds it inside

parts.note: he stands for any male fellow

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man spins round and seizes a gin-based drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn on' reads as a fellow switching something on; it means depend upon. 'cocktail' gives ING, which 'grabbing' places in the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinge on something is to depend or turn upon it.

clue.text: Host investing stronghold in target area

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, here the castle tower goes inside the target ring

parts.note: the inner is the ring next to the bull on a target
a keep is the main fortified tower of a castle

explanation.surface: An army invests a fortress inside a target zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The INNER is the ring of an archery or darts target just outside the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper is the landlord who hosts guests at an inn.

clue.text: Walk by the sea pleased an invalid

indicators.note: invalid means not sound, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside stroll delighted a convalescent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' looks like a sick person, but signals the anagram of PLEASED AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade, often along the seafront.

clue.text: English fashion in catalogue is an example to copy

indicators.note: the first two pieces go in the list word

parts.note: a roll is a list or register
mode is fashion or style

explanation.surface: An English designer's look in a catalogue becomes the one to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look up to and imitate.

clue.text: Stays to the end, backing gripping speaker

indicators.note: the outer piece grips the other, holding it inside
going backwards, so the letters of the aim word are read in reverse

parts.note: an end or goal is an aim
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Someone stays to the end, supporting a riveting speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AIM into MIA, which grips ORATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria are suspensions or postponements, as when a court stays proceedings.

clue.text: Strive in order to secure one's come back

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so the letter for one goes inside
putting letters in order means rearranging them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Struggling to make sure of a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges STRIVE; 'to secure' places I among the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit a place is to return to it.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer with pawn delayed riposte

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

indicators.note: a riposte is a return, so the word for delayed is turned back

parts.note: delayed means late

explanation.surface: A chess player makes a late reply after moving a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riposte' (a return) turns the word for delayed back to ETAL. 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one segment of a flower's corolla, part of something that blooms.

clue.text: Monarch with retinue going round country

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a train is a monarch's retinue of attendants
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen travels the land with her attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps the retinue around the monarch; ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land or countryside.

clue.text: Fancy opponents have not lost face

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N
a visage is a face

explanation.surface: Imagine the rival team managing to save face.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit North, South, East and West; North and East are on opposite sides. 'have not lost' is linking padding in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or picture it.

clue.text: Provide funds for daughter old enough to comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend can mean to include or contain, so the daughter letter goes inside

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough

explanation.surface: A parent funds a daughter now she is old enough to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehend' means understand on the surface but contain here.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow a college or person is to give them a permanent income.

clue.text: Worsted Russian

definitions.meaning: a twilled cloth spun from worsted wool
a man's name, the French form of Sergei used for Russians

explanation.surface: A Russian who has been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worsted' reads as defeated; it is a woollen yarn, and serge is a worsted fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth; Serge is a common Russian given name.

clue.text: Grass, whichever way one looks

indicators.note: reading from either direction gives the same word, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Grass stretching in every direction one looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes.

clue.text: Absence of line in fashion causes irritation to viewer

indicators.note: absence means something is missing, so the letter for line is removed

parts.note: a style is a fashion

explanation.surface: A lack of line in fashion design annoys onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absence of' removes L from STYLE. 'Viewer' is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a source of eye discomfort.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps doubly likely to flee?

parts.note: a soldier who deserts runs off from duty
to rat is to run out on one's side, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A soldier twice as inclined to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' says two words for fleeing are joined; the Desert Rats were British soldiers of the 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert Rats was the nickname of the British 7th Armoured Division, so one member is a soldier.

clue.text: A charge for present

parts.note: a ward is a person in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A fee levied for a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize or gift presented.

clue.text: Quick intelligence keeping lady on horseback

indicators.note: one piece keeps another inside it

parts.note: having your wits about you means quick intelligence
her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: A clever woman keeps her seat while riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the withers are the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades, a part found on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: The withers are the highest point of a horse's back, at the base of the mane.

clue.text: Unchanging rental negotiated after first quarter

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the compass letter

parts.note: east, E, is the first of the compass quarters as usually listed

indicators.note: negotiated terms are worked out, so the letters of rental are reworked

explanation.surface: The rent stays fixed after the first quarter's negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges rental to TERNAL, placed 'after' the compass letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever without alteration.
